newsitem.title: USA: Naming Martian rocks is child's play for NASA.
newsitem.headline: Naming Martian rocks is child's play for NASA.

text.p: When it comes to names, the people at the National Aeronautics and Space Administration are notorious for coming up with long, complicated terms for relatively simple mechanisms.

So in a mission with enough scientific terms to fill a dictionary, it comes as a surprise to learn that NASA scientists at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, California, have given some of the rocks around the landing site such simple monikers as Barnacle Bill, Yogi, Flat Top and Casper.
Matthew Golombek, one of the project scientists on the $266 million Pathfinder mission, said the decision to deviate from standard operating procedure was not very difficult.

"It's easier than saying, 'That rock over there with the little things on it,'" Golombek said. "The idea to use names is really to help us refer to the rocks among ourselves, and if you can a little fun with it, why not?"

Barnacle Bill is a multicolored rock with apparent projections on the surface. Yogi, a much larger rock several meters from the landing site, is named after the animated television character Yogi Bear. Flat Top, not surprisingly, is a flattish rock, while Casper appears to be white, like Casper the Friendly Ghost of comic book fame.
So far at least a dozen rocks have names, and more are expected in the days ahead.

The Pathfinder lander itself was renamed Saturday after the late NASA scientist and best-selling author Carl Sagan. And the Sojourner, the roving explorer that will drive along the planet's surface, was named after an African-American crusader, Sojourner Truth, who fought against slavery and worked for the Union army during the Civil War.

But just to prove that old habits die hard at NASA, the scientists at JPL have decided to keep calling the device that will allow Sojourner to probe the characteristics of Mars an alpha proton X-ray spectrometer.
